 November 2026 income tax deadlines: ITR due date for audit … 
 Tax Insights
 By Anjali Anand 
 Nov 04, 2026
 November 2026 income tax deadlines: ITR due date for audit cases on November 21, TDS and transfer pricing filings
 Source: Shutterstock

 Highlights 
 TDS and TCS deducted in October 2026, along with STT and CTT collected that month, are due for deposit by November 7.
 The CBDT has extended the ITR deadline for specified audit cases for AY 2026-27 from October 31 to November 21, 2026.
 Taxpayers covered by transfer pricing provisions have a separate November 30 deadline.
 The extension is not general; salaried individuals and taxpayers outside audit provisions are not covered.
 Introduction 
 Businesses, firms and tax deductors face a packed compliance calendar this month, with five key dates between November 7 and November 30, 2026. The most closely watched is November 21, the extended income tax return deadline for taxpayers covered by audit provisions for assessment year 2026-27.
 The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) moved that deadline from October 31. Earlier, the due date for tax audit reports was shifted from September 30 to October 21.
 Why Investors Are Watching 
 The November 21 deadline applies to corporate taxpayers, non-corporate taxpayers whose accounts must be audited, and partners of firms subject to audit, including the spouse of such a partner where the Portuguese Civil Code applies. Form 3CEFB, used to opt for safe harbour rules on specified domestic transactions, and other reports whose original due date was October 31 also fall due on this date where applicable.
 The extension is targeted. Salaried individuals and taxpayers not covered by audit provisions are not part of it, and taxpayers under transfer pricing provisions have a separate deadline of November 30.
 Market Context 
 The month opens with deposit obligations. By November 7, deductors must deposit TDS and TCS deducted or collected in October 2026, while securities transaction tax (STT) and commodities transaction tax (CTT) collected in October must also be deposited. Government offices that pay tax without a challan must transfer the amount to the Centre on the same day, and buyers submit Form 127 declarations for purchases made without tax collection at source, where applicable.
 Equity market activity, which drives STT collections, stayed firm into November. Foreign institutions bought about ₹6,836.81 crore of Indian equities on November 3, and the Nifty 50 recovered to 23,876 by 9:19 am on November 4 after a lower open.
 What Market Participants Will Monitor 
 Certificates come next. Form 132, the TDS certificate for tax deducted in September 2026, is due by November 14. By November 15, deductors must issue Form 133 for TCS and Form 131 for specified non-salary TDS for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Government offices file Form 137, the TDS/TCS book adjustment statement for October, by the same date.
 Stock exchanges also have a filing on November 15: Form 1, the monthly statement of transactions where client codes were modified after registration during October. On November 30, taxpayers required to furnish an accountant's report under section 92E must file their AY 2026-27 returns.
 Industry or Peer Perspective 
 The calendar affects a wide range of taxpayers rather than one company. Stock exchanges have a direct filing obligation through Form 1, and BSE is among the companies scheduled to report September-quarter results on November 4, but peer relevance is otherwise limited based on the available information.
 Several deadlines apply only to specific categories, and taxpayers are advised to verify the forms that apply to them on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal.
 Conclusion 
 November 2026 compresses deposit, certificate and return deadlines into a few weeks, with November 21 for audit cases and November 30 for transfer pricing cases as the two main return dates.
 With the CBDT having already extended both audit-report and return timelines this season, the focus now shifts to filings being completed within the revised windows.
